From the Buyer’s perspective, the principal points to address are the purchase price, the closing timetable, and the very limited representations package. We will be proposing a materially lower price, a longer and more flexible closing period, and a fuller set of seller reps, warranties, and customary buyer protections, including indemnity and escrow mechanics.

We will revert with markup shortly, but please note at a high level that the current draft will need significant revisions before it can be taken forward.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.private_reasoning: Seller should move slightly on price and timing to keep negotiations alive, but resist a wholesale expansion of the reps/indemnity package. I have made modest concessions: reduced price from the opening ask, extended closing to 60 days with a mutual cooperation framework, expanded confidentiality to cover permitted recipients only under confidentiality obligations, and broadened the reps somewhat while keeping them limited and seller-protective. I have not agreed to escrow/holdback, baskets, caps, or an uncapped indemnity regime, and I have kept the seller knowledge qualifier unless the Buyer can propose a principled formulation. This should signal willingness to progress without giving away the key economics or risk allocation.

Dear Counsel,

Thank you for your note. We have revised the draft to reflect a more balanced starting point and to move the process forward. In particular, we have made some movement on economics and timing, and we have expanded the seller disclosure package to include the core fundamental matters that are customary for this transaction.

That said, we have not adopted an open-ended buyer protection package, and we would not expect the draft to carry all of the items you mention absent a more developed diligence record and agreement on commercial parameters. We think the revised draft provides a workable basis for your markup, and we remain happy to discuss the outstanding points once we have seen your proposed revisions.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, subject to any adjustments expressly set out in this Agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on a date falling no later than 60 days after signing (or such later date as the parties may agree in writing), provided that the Buyer has used commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy any conditions precedent within its control and the parties have in good faith cooperated to obtain any required regulatory approvals, third-party consents, and financing-related deliverables reasonably necessary for Closing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer, as of the date of this Agreement and as of Closing (except where expressly stated otherwise), that: (a) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) it has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of any liens or encumbrances other than those created by the Buyer or contemplated by this Agreement; (c) the capitalization of the Company is as set out in the disclosure schedules; and (d) to the Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements delivered to the Buyer are accurate in all material respects and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition of the Company. For purposes of this Agreement, “knowledge” means the actual knowledge of those officers of the Seller and the Company responsible for the relevant matter after making reasonable inquiry of the persons within the Seller’s and Company’s organization who would reasonably be expected to have knowledge of such matter.

The Seller shall also provide customary, limited representations regarding (i) the absence of undisclosed liabilities other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business, (ii) compliance with law in all material respects, (iii) material contracts listed on the disclosure schedules, (iv) no pending or threatened litigation known to the Seller, (v) taxes for the periods expressly covered in the disclosure schedules, (vi) employees and benefit matters in all material respects, and (vii) ownership or valid license of material intellectual property and material data/privacy compliance in all material respects. No representation is made as to any matter not expressly stated in this Agreement, and no implied representations are given.
For avoidance of doubt, no representation or warranty shall be deemed made regarding any material adverse effect except to the extent expressly and specifically set forth in this Agreement.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except as disclosure is required by law or regulation, to the parties’ respective legal, tax, accounting, financial, insurance, and other professional advisers on a need-to-know basis under duties of confidentiality, to each party’s affiliates, financing sources, and actual or prospective investors or insurers involved in the transaction under customary confidentiality obligations, and to governmental or regulatory authorities as required in connection with the transaction; provided that no disclosure shall be made other than on a confidential basis to the extent practicable.

receiver.requested_changes:
1) Price: reduce the purchase price from USD 42,500,000 further (Buyer’s opening markup should move materially below this figure).
2) Closing: extend the outside date beyond 60 days and delete/soften any obligation that Buyer must use ‘commercially reasonable efforts’ for matters outside its control; Buyer should only be required to use efforts for items squarely within its control.
3) Seller reps: expand and make them more robust, including at minimum authority, title, capitalization, no undisclosed liabilities, compliance with law, material contracts, litigation, taxes, employees/benefits, IP, and data/privacy, with knowledge qualifiers only where truly appropriate.
4) Knowledge standard: narrow the seller knowledge definition and require named knowledge persons, actual knowledge, and reasonable inquiry.
5) No-implied-reps language: strike or soften the blanket disclaimer so it does not undermine agreed disclosures or fundamental protections.
6) Confidentiality: ensure the clause permits disclosures to financing sources and insurers only on customary confidentiality terms, without overbroad restrictions on required disclosures.
7) Add standard buyer protections in the draft (to the extent not yet included): bring-down condition, no material adverse change qualifier, and appropriate closing deliverables from Seller.
receiver.message_back: Thank you. We appreciate the movement on price and timing, but the draft remains too seller-protective for Buyer to treat as a workable near-final. We will circulate our markup shortly, but you should expect us to push further on economics, closing mechanics, and the scope/quality of the seller representations. In particular, we will be seeking broader fundamental and business reps, a narrower knowledge standard, and more balanced closing and disclosure mechanics. We remain available to discuss once you have had a chance to review our revisions.
